narrativeReportMd:
# MedicinalProduct R4->R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
R4 `MedicinalProduct` is a breaking migration to R6: the same-named resource is absent and the practical successor is `MedicinalProductDefinition`. The resource identity change is the highest-impact break, and several local elements were removed, renamed, rewrapped, or split into other R6 product-definition resources.

## Scope
I analyzed the R4 `StructureDefinition-MedicinalProduct` and the R6 `StructureDefinition-MedicinalProductDefinition` successor, with targeted inspection of related R6 definition resources to understand split destinations. Inherited `Resource`, `DomainResource`, and `BackboneElement` changes are excluded.

## Main migration themes
The migration is graph-level, not just field-level. Product identity changes from `MedicinalProduct` to `MedicinalProductDefinition`; package, pharmaceutical, authorization, clinical-use, ingredient, and operation details are distributed across `PackagedProductDefinition`, `AdministrableProductDefinition`, `ManufacturedItemDefinition`, `Ingredient`, `ClinicalUseDefinition`, and `RegulatedAuthorization`. Several same-looking or similar fields also change JSON shape, including package references, contacts, cross-references, coded values, and operations.

## Highest-impact findings
The root identity rename (`MedicinalProduct:ARTIFACT_IDENTITY:root:3d7f2a`) makes all untransformed R4 instances invalid in R6. The removed/split `pharmaceuticalProduct`, package, manufacturing operation, and special designation structures carry the largest data migration risk because they often require creating or linking separate R6 resources rather than moving a scalar value.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important for split resources and ambiguous semantics: pharmaceutical-product decomposition, special designations, manufacturing authorization/regulator data, cross-reference identifiers, terminology normalization for name language, and preservation of R6-only modifier status during downgrade.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Many breaks could have been softened with deprecated aliases or choice elements, but that would duplicate the new normalized product-definition model. R6 appears to prioritize cleaner resource boundaries and richer semantics over wire compatibility with the R4 draft resource family.

## Follow-up analysis
Separate reports should assess `PackagedProductDefinition`, `AdministrableProductDefinition`, `ManufacturedItemDefinition`, `Ingredient`, `ClinicalUseDefinition`, `RegulatedAuthorization`, and relevant base/datatype artifacts for their own breaking changes.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: R4 `MedicinalProduct` has a high-confidence R6 successor `MedicinalProductDefinition`, but the migration is hard-breaking. Top concerns are the resourceType/canonical rename, graph-level splits for package/pharmaceutical/authorization data, and same-name fields whose JSON type changed. The main uncertainty is exact official mapping for split resources because no official diff or ConceptMap was available locally.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should start with a root resource rename and reference retargeting, then apply local field transforms. Simple path rewrites handle some data (`productClassification` -> `classification`, `paediatricUseIndicator` -> `pediatricUseIndicator`, name substructure renames), but package, pharmaceutical, operation, and special-designation data often require creating related R6 resources. R6-to-R4 downgrade must preserve modifier `status` and R6-only content through extensions or sidecar mappings if round-trip fidelity matters.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for the presence, type, cardinality, binding, and flag differences because they come directly from local core StructureDefinitions and package indexes. Confidence is medium for some migration destinations because those are inferred from related R6 resource definitions rather than an official R4-to-R6 mapping or narrative migration guide.

findings.title: R4 MedicinalProduct has no same-named R6 resource; successor is MedicinalProductDefinition

oldState.summary: R4 defines a concrete resource type MedicinalProduct.

semanticText.definition: Detailed definition of a medicinal product, typically for regulatory use.

oldState.narrativeMd: `StructureDefinition/MedicinalProduct` exists in R4 with `type` and JSON `resourceType` of `MedicinalProduct`.

newState.summary: The R6 package has no StructureDefinition-MedicinalProduct; the close successor is MedicinalProductDefinition.

semanticText.definition: MedicinalProductDefinition is the R6 product definition resource.

newState.narrativeMd: The R6 package index contains `StructureDefinition-MedicinalProductDefinition` and no `StructureDefinition-MedicinalProduct`. The canonical URL, type code, generated class name, REST resource name, and instance `resourceType` all change.

facts.note: Maturity/status changed, but the breaking aspect is identity.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `MedicinalProductDefinition` preserves the product-definition scope, shares many local elements (`identifier`, `type`, `domain`, `name`, `marketingStatus`, documents, and contacts), and is the only R6 StructureDefinition indexed with the `MedicinalProduct` stem.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct instance and API break. A conformant R4 JSON resource has `resourceType: "MedicinalProduct"`; an R6 validator expecting core R6 resources will not accept that resource type because the R6 resource name is `MedicinalProductDefinition`. Generated models, REST endpoints, search parameters, subscriptions, FHIRPath expressions, and authorization rules keyed by resource type must all be updated.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Medicinal product records are regulatory/business-critical. Misclassifying or dropping the product resource during migration can break downstream authorization, packaging, and clinical-use links.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal of separating definitional medicinal products from clinical `Medication` and aligning the product-definition family is reasonable. However, the R4 `MedicinalProduct` resource was already a definitional regulatory product resource, so the identity-level rename to `MedicinalProductDefinition` is not clearly necessary to meet the semantic goal. The root break was therefore probably avoidable even if later field-level remodels were still needed.
justification.inferredGoal: Separate definitional medicinal-product resources from clinical Medication instances and align naming with the R6 product-definition family.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `MedicinalProduct` as the R6 successor resource name and clarify that it is a product-definition resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would have kept the resource type and canonical identity as `MedicinalProduct`, updated the definition to make the product-definition role explicit, and applied content-model changes separately. That would preserve old `resourceType` values, many references, generated class names, and REST discriminators. The tradeoff is a less tidy name in a family that otherwise uses `*Definition`, but that is a moderate naming/tooling cost rather than evidence that the breaking identity change was required.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve resourceType and canonical compatibility but leave a less consistent name beside the R6 `*Definition` resource family.

evidence.detail: The R6 successor defines `id`, `name`, and `type` as `MedicinalProductDefinition`.
The R6 package index contains `StructureDefinition-MedicinalProductDefinition.json` and no `StructureDefinition-MedicinalProduct.json` entry.

examples.examplesMd: The example is intentionally minimal but includes the R4 mandatory `name.productName`. The local element findings below still matter after the root `resourceType` is renamed.

findings.narrativeMd: The assigned R4 artifact is not carried forward under the same resource identity. R6 uses `MedicinalProductDefinition`, so migration is not just a field-level transform: resource type strings, canonical URLs, generated class names, REST compartments/endpoints, search parameter names, and references from related resources must be retargeted.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An otherwise valid R4 instance with `resourceType: "MedicinalProduct"` is not an R6 `MedicinalProductDefinition` instance. Conversely, a valid R6 `MedicinalProductDefinition` cannot be represented in R4 without changing the resource type and handling R6-only fields. Strict parsers and schema/codegen systems will fail before reaching element-level validation.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Introduce an explicit resource-level transform from `MedicinalProduct` to `MedicinalProductDefinition`, then apply the element-level mappings in this report. Update reference targets, REST routes, generated model names, search definitions, and any persistence discriminators keyed by resource type. Keep regression fixtures for resourceType-only rejection, successful migrated root identity, and references from related product-definition resources.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The rename could have been less disruptive with a deprecated alias or compatibility profile, but FHIR core resource identity is intentionally explicit. The practical mitigation is a documented cross-version mapping and possibly cross-version extensions for data that no longer has a direct R6 element.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The successor mapping is high-confidence but inferred from local package contents rather than an official R4-to-R6 diff page.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `MedicinalProduct` is not present as an R6 resource; the apparent successor is `MedicinalProductDefinition`. This is more than an element migration: instances, REST/resource-type discriminators, generated model classes, profile canonicals, references, and FHIRPath/search logic keyed by the resource name all need a rename. Even with low FMM, the resource was already described in R4 as a detailed regulatory product definition, so the semantic need for a new base resource identity is not obvious. Keeping the `MedicinalProduct` identity while clarifying its product-definition role looks like a plausible lower-cost base design, so the identity change deserves renewed attention.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition-MedicinalProduct has id/type/url `MedicinalProduct`; R6 package index has `StructureDefinition-MedicinalProductDefinition` and no same-named MedicinalProduct StructureDefinition.
R4 root definition: detailed medicinal product definition, typically for regulatory use; R6 MedicinalProductDefinition definition covers the same regulatory/product-definition role.
EMA SPOR/PMS public page says HL7 FHIR replaces XEVPRM for ISO IDMP medicinal product data submission; HL7 ePI Type 2 guide uses MedicinalProductDefinition as the product resource chain anchor.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 0 and trial-use status substantially soften the stability expectation, and the quick search did not prove broad installed R4 `MedicinalProduct` deployment. They do not eliminate concern because this is a top-level resource identity break for regulatory medicinal product data, a domain with documented FHIR/IDMP implementation relevance.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: the resource type, canonical URL, generated class, REST endpoint, references, and discriminators change; old `resourceType: MedicinalProduct` instances are also new-invalid without a transform.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Yes. A base R6 design could have retained `MedicinalProduct` as the resource identity and updated the definition/content model to match the product-definition family. The tradeoff is less tidy naming beside other `*Definition` resources, but that is modest compared with a resource identity break.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: Agree with the existing Critical impact and Yes alternative judgment, but the fresh rationale relies less on presumed prevalence and more on the avoidability of the resource identity rename despite low FMM.

findings.title: pharmaceuticalProduct reference was removed and split across other product-definition resources

oldState.narrativeMd: `MedicinalProduct.pharmaceuticalProduct` directly linked pharmaceutical aspects of the product to one or more `MedicinalProductPharmaceutical` resources.

newState.summary: No same element exists on MedicinalProductDefinition; related concepts are modeled by comprisedOf and separate AdministrableProductDefinition, ManufacturedItemDefinition, and Ingredient resources.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 `MedicinalProductDefinition.comprisedOf` points to manufactured items/devices, while `AdministrableProductDefinition.formOf` points back to the product and carries administrable-dose-form/route details. Ingredients may also point in with `Ingredient.for`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R4 target `MedicinalProductPharmaceutical` is absent in R6. The closest R6 resources distribute its concepts across administrable, manufactured, ingredient, and device definitions; this is a split rather than a simple rename.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 instance containing `pharmaceuticalProduct` remains invalid after only the resource rename because R6 has no such element on `MedicinalProductDefinition`. The migration is semantically significant because the old reference may need to become one or more new resources and/or inverse links rather than a single local child reference.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Pharmaceutical form, route, ingredient, and device composition are key regulatory data. Lossy conversion can affect product equivalence and authorization workflows.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal of splitting pharmaceutical, administrable, manufactured, ingredient, and device aspects into more precise resources is reasonable and the old single reference was too coarse for that model. A compatibility element could reduce disruption, but it would not fully preserve the old graph unless the removed target resource or a precise target mapping were also retained. Given that material duplication and mapping burden, the breaking split is probably justified.
justification.inferredGoal: Separate administrable, manufactured, ingredient, and device aspects into dedicated definition resources.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain a deprecated `pharmaceuticalProduct` reference while adding normalized R6 product-definition relationships.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could have kept `pharmaceuticalProduct` as a deprecated reference and added the R6 normalized links. That would preserve R4 product instances containing the field, at least at the local element level. The alternative is incomplete because the old `MedicinalProductPharmaceutical` target is also absent in R6, and it creates two same-resource or same-graph representations for overlapping pharmaceutical facts that could diverge and persist indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves common old links but duplicates pharmaceutical facts across legacy references and newer administrable, manufactured, ingredient, or device resources.

evidence.detail: No `MedicinalProductDefinition.pharmaceuticalProduct` element exists; R6 adds `comprisedOf` for manufactured items/devices.
`formOf` references `MedicinalProductDefinition` and carries administrable product details.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example is illustrative only. A real transform must inspect the referenced R4 `MedicinalProductPharmaceutical` and decide whether data belongs in `AdministrableProductDefinition`, `ManufacturedItemDefinition`, `Ingredient`, `DeviceDefinition`, or multiple resources.

findings.narrativeMd: `pharmaceuticalProduct` is a local R4 element whose target resource family was remodeled in R6. This is hard-breaking for instances and generated code because the field disappears, and it is not a simple field rename because the destination depends on what the referenced pharmaceutical resource was expressing.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 content containing `pharmaceuticalProduct` is old-valid/new-invalid unless transformed. R6 content may be represented by separate resources and inverse references, so an R6 graph cannot be collapsed back into the R4 single reference without potential loss or heuristic reconstruction.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Resolve each referenced `MedicinalProductPharmaceutical` before migration. Create or link `AdministrableProductDefinition` for administrable dose form and route, `ManufacturedItemDefinition` for manufactured items, `Ingredient` for detailed ingredients, and `DeviceDefinition` where applicable. Test multi-component and device-combination products explicitly.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible path could have retained the old reference as deprecated while adding normalized R6 links. That would be easier for R4 data but would allow two competing ways to say the same thing, so a clean split is understandable but disruptive.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Exact mapping requires analysis of the referenced R4 target resources, which is outside this single-artifact report.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `MedicinalProduct.pharmaceuticalProduct` was a repeating reference to `MedicinalProductPharmaceutical`; R6 has no same local element and the related information is distributed across `MedicinalProductDefinition.comprisedOf`, `AdministrableProductDefinition.formOf`, `Ingredient.for`, and related definition resources. Existing instances using the element need a graph-level migration, not a simple path rename. That is a real break for validators and SDKs, but the R6 split gives more precise administrable, manufactured, ingredient, and device modeling. Preserving the old local reference in base R6 would only be partial unless the removed target resource or a precise legacy target mapping were also retained.
keyEvidence: R4 element `MedicinalProduct.pharmaceuticalProduct` is 0..* Reference(MedicinalProductPharmaceutical).

R6 MedicinalProductDefinition has `comprisedOf` Reference(ManufacturedItemDefinition|DeviceDefinition), while AdministrableProductDefinition.formOf and Ingredient.for point back to MedicinalProductDefinition.
R6 package uses separate AdministrableProductDefinition, ManufacturedItemDefinition, Ingredient, and DeviceDefinition resources for concepts formerly associated with pharmaceutical-product detail.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use lowers the expectation that the old element shape must be preserved. The domain is regulatory and implementation-relevant, but the evidence checked was broad medicinal-product use rather than specific production use of the R4 `pharmaceuticalProduct` path.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: after the resource rename, an R4 instance containing `pharmaceuticalProduct` still has an element that R6 MedicinalProductDefinition does not allow; migration can require new related resources and inverse links.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial. A deprecated `pharmaceuticalProduct` element could reduce immediate breakage, but it would need a legacy target resource or target mapping and would duplicate facts across old pharmaceutical-product references and the normalized R6 resource graph.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: Agree with the existing High impact and Partial alternative judgment, with FMM 0 tempering the prevalence assumptions.

findings.title: packagedMedicinalProduct changed from package resource references to a package-type CodeableConcept

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 linked from the product to package resources using references.

newState.summary: R6 element is 0..* CodeableConcept describing package type; detailed packages are separate PackagedProductDefinition resources that point back with packageFor.
newState.narrativeMd: `MedicinalProductDefinition.packagedMedicinalProduct` no longer carries a resource reference. The detailed package model lives in `PackagedProductDefinition.packageFor`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element name is retained, but its type and semantics changed. The package resource successor is `PackagedProductDefinition`, which references the product from the package side.

impact.impactRationaleMd: A JSON array of FHIR `Reference` objects is not a valid `CodeableConcept` array. Existing R4 instances and generated accessors expecting package references will fail after the root resource rename. R6 package details also require a graph-level migration to `PackagedProductDefinition` rather than an in-place element conversion.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Packaging information can affect regulatory authorization, dispensing, inventory, and supply-chain behavior.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of separating a product-level package type from detailed package definition resources is plausible and semantically clearer than the R4 product-to-package reference alone. A less-breaking model could have avoided reusing the old element name for a different type, but fully preserving R4 graphs would also require a clear successor for `MedicinalProductPackaged`. Because the compatibility path has substantial duplicate-representation and graph-consistency tradeoffs, the break is probably justified.
justification.inferredGoal: Distinguish package type from detailed package resources and move detailed packages into `PackagedProductDefinition`.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add a new package-type element while retaining the old package-resource reference shape for transition.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design would have kept `packagedMedicinalProduct` as a package-resource reference, added a distinct `packageType` CodeableConcept, and linked detailed R6 package resources separately. This would preserve old JSON shapes better than changing `packagedMedicinalProduct` from `Reference` to `CodeableConcept`. The cost is that package type, package references, and inverse `PackagedProductDefinition.packageFor` links can become inconsistent, and implementers may have to maintain both old and new representations for a long transition.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids the same-name type break but duplicates package summary/detail relationships and complicates alignment with `PackagedProductDefinition.packageFor`.

evidence.detail: R6 type is `CodeableConcept` with an example package-type value set.

examples.examplesMd: Detailed package data should normally be migrated to a separate `PackagedProductDefinition` with `packageFor` pointing at the migrated product. The shown `CodeableConcept` is only the product-level package type.

findings.narrativeMd: The element name survived but its meaning did not: R4 stored links to package resources, while R6 stores package type codes and expects detailed package resources elsewhere. This is a high-risk codegen trap because a same-named property changes from `Reference[]` to `CodeableConcept[]`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 `Reference` object in `packagedMedicinalProduct` is invalid in R6. An R6 package-type code can be represented only awkwardly in R4 unless a separate `MedicinalProductPackaged` resource is created or an extension is used.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For each old package reference, migrate the referenced package resource to `PackagedProductDefinition` and set `packageFor` to the migrated product. Populate `MedicinalProductDefinition.packagedMedicinalProduct` only when a package-type classification is known. Test that old package references are not accidentally serialized as CodeableConcepts.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A non-breaking alternative would have been an added `packageType` element and a deprecated retained package reference. R6 instead reused the old element name for a different type, which is more disruptive for generated code and JSON transforms.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The path name `packagedMedicinalProduct` survives, but its value changes from a Reference to a package resource in R4 to a CodeableConcept package type in R6. Detailed package records are instead represented by `PackagedProductDefinition` resources that point back with `packageFor`. This is a hard JSON shape and generated-API break for old instances that used package references. The R6 distinction between a package type summary and separate package-definition resources is understandable, and keeping both the old direct reference model and the new inverse package graph in base R6 would create duplicate package relationships and consistency rules.
keyEvidence: R4 `MedicinalProduct.packagedMedicinalProduct` is 0..* Reference(MedicinalProductPackaged).
R6 `MedicinalProductDefinition.packagedMedicinalProduct` is 0..* CodeableConcept with package-type binding.
R6 `PackagedProductDefinition.packageFor` is 0..* Reference(MedicinalProductDefinition).
freshReview.fmmEffect: Low FMM softens the break, particularly because no path-specific production evidence was found. Packaging data is still regulatory and supply-chain relevant, so the break is real but not enough by itself to override the R6 normalization goal.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: old Reference array items are not valid CodeableConcept array items, and package detail moves to a related resource graph.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial. R6 could have kept a package-reference element and added a distinct package-type element, but that would leave direct and inverse package relationships that can diverge and would complicate validation and migration.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: Agree with the existing High impact and Partial alternative judgment, though the fresh review treats the break as proportionate for FMM 0 content.

findings.title: contact changed from direct Reference to a backbone with mandatory contact reference

oldState.narrativeMd: Each array item was a reference directly under `MedicinalProduct.contact`.

newState.summary: R6 `contact` is 0..* BackboneElement with optional `type` and mandatory `contact` Reference(Organization|PractitionerRole).
newState.narrativeMd: The actual reference moved one level down to `contact.contact`; `contact.type` can classify the contact role.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The short/definition text and reference target profiles are preserved; the representation is wrapped in a new backbone to add contact role/type metadata.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Old direct reference array items are not valid R6 backbone array items. The transform is usually deterministic, but parsers, generated models, and FHIRPath expressions must be updated from `contact` to `contact.contact`.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Contact routing errors can affect pharmacovigilance and regulatory communication workflows, though the data can usually be migrated losslessly.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding per-contact role or type metadata is a reasonable R6 goal, and the new backbone is a clean first-class representation. The old shape could be preserved only by using extensions on references, parallel metadata, or a distinct typed-contact structure alongside the old `contact` field. Those alternatives reduce wire breakage but have meaningful discoverability, validation, and duplication costs, so the backbone redesign is probably justified rather than fully avoidable.
justification.inferredGoal: Add contact role/type metadata to each product contact.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep direct `contact` references and add typed-contact metadata through a separate backbone or governed extension.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base option would have retained `contact` as `Reference(Organization|PractitionerRole)` and added a distinct typed-contact mechanism. That would preserve most R4 instances with contacts. It is only a partial alternative because extension-based type metadata is less interoperable, while a separate first-class typed-contact backbone leaves two ways to carry a product contact and risks indefinite divergence.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves simple references but either hides contact type in extensions or creates duplicate contact representations.

evidence.detail: R4 `contact` is `Reference` to Organization or PractitionerRole.
R6 `contact.contact` is mandatory within each contact backbone and has the same target profiles.

examples.examplesMd: The local transform can be lossless when the old item is a normal `Reference`; optional contact type can be added from local business rules if known.

findings.narrativeMd: `contact` is a same-name but different-shape element. Implementers who only rename the resource will still emit invalid R6 because the reference must be nested in a backbone item.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old direct references are old-valid/new-invalid. R6 contact backbones can be projected back to R4 by dropping `contact.type` and moving `contact.contact` up, but that loses the R6 contact classification.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap each old `contact` Reference as `{ "contact": <old Reference> }`. Update generated models, FHIRPath, search extraction, and tests to account for the new backbone. Decide whether any local contact-role data should populate `contact.type`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Adding `contact.type` as an extension on the old repeating Reference would have been backward-compatible but less discoverable. The backbone is a reasonable design choice with a straightforward migration.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `contact` was a direct Reference list; R6 wraps each contact in a backbone with optional `type` and required `contact`. Old JSON reference objects are not valid R6 backbone entries, and generated accessors/FHIRPath paths move from `contact` to `contact.contact`. The transform is usually deterministic, and the new structure has a clear goal: per-contact role/type metadata. For a low-FMM trial-use resource, this wrapper break appears proportionate.
keyEvidence: R4 `MedicinalProduct.contact` is 0..* Reference(Organization|PractitionerRole).
R6 `MedicinalProductDefinition.contact` is 0..* BackboneElement with `contact.contact` 1..1 Reference(Organization|PractitionerRole).
R6 adds `contact.type` CodeableConcept for product contact classification.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use softens the stability concern. Contacts can matter for regulatory communication, but the path-level migration is low-loss and no quick evidence showed heavy R4-path-specific production use.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: old Reference items must be wrapped as backbone entries; runtime/API/codegen paths also change.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial. Keeping direct references plus adding type metadata via extensions or a parallel typed-contact element would preserve old instances but either hides important metadata or creates two contact representations.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: Agree with the existing Medium impact and Partial alternative judgment.

findings.title: crossReference changed from Identifier to a typed backbone with mandatory CodeableReference product

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 could record another product by business identifier only.

newState.summary: R6 `crossReference` is 0..* BackboneElement with mandatory `product` CodeableReference(MedicinalProductDefinition) and optional relationship `type`.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 can identify the related product by reference or concept and can classify the relationship.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The retained element name and definition identify this as the same business concept, but the R6 representation is richer and not wire-compatible.

impact.impactRationaleMd: An R4 `Identifier` object is not a valid R6 `crossReference` backbone. Mapping can often place the identifier in `product.reference.identifier`, but implementers must choose whether the old identifier denoted a concrete product reference, a codeable concept, or a local business relationship.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrect cross-product linkage can affect equivalence, branded/generic relationships, investigational-to-authorized product tracing, and parallel import logic.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of making cross-product relationships typed and capable of pointing at actual product-definition resources is reasonable. The R4 bare `Identifier` form was ambiguous, and a fully compatible design would have to preserve that ambiguity beside the richer relationship model. Because the alternative would cover common legacy cases but weaken the clarity of the new model, the breaking change is probably justified.
justification.inferredGoal: Make product cross-references typed and capable of pointing at actual product-definition resources.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the bare identifier form while adding a typed related-product backbone or relationship fields.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could have kept `crossReference` as a repeating `Identifier` and added optional relationship type and product reference fields under a new element. This would preserve existing identifier-only instances. It is incomplete because it does not resolve whether the old identifier denotes a product, relationship, or local business key, and it creates validation ambiguity when both the old identifier and the new typed relationship are present.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves legacy identifiers but continues ambiguous relationships and duplicates related-product representations.

evidence.detail: R6 adds optional relationship type with an example value set.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example uses `Reference.identifier` inside `CodeableReference.reference`; a local system might instead resolve the identifier to an actual `MedicinalProductDefinition/{id}` reference.

findings.narrativeMd: `crossReference` moved from a lightweight identifier list to a structured relationship. That improves meaning but breaks wire compatibility and may expose ambiguous old data where the relationship type or target product cannot be resolved.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 identifier array items become invalid in R6. R6 backbones can be partially represented in R4 only by dropping relationship `type` and reducing `product` to an identifier, which may lose target-reference and relationship semantics.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Attempt to resolve each old identifier to a migrated `MedicinalProductDefinition`; if resolution is not possible, carry it as `product.reference.identifier` and flag for review. Populate `crossReference.type` only where the old business context makes the relationship clear.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible alternative would have added `crossReference.product` and `crossReference.type` while retaining bare identifiers. R6 chose a more coherent backbone, but existing data needs an explicit mapping policy.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `crossReference` was a bare Identifier; R6 makes `crossReference` a backbone with mandatory `product` CodeableReference and optional relationship `type`. Existing identifier-only entries are invalid without wrapping and semantic interpretation. The new design resolves a real ambiguity by making the related product and relationship type explicit. Because the old Identifier did not say whether it identified a product, relationship, or local business key, preserving it in base R6 would keep the ambiguity and duplicate the clearer relationship model.
keyEvidence: R4 `MedicinalProduct.crossReference` is 0..* Identifier.
R6 `MedicinalProductDefinition.crossReference.product` is 1..1 CodeableReference(MedicinalProductDefinition).
R6 `crossReference.type` definition covers branded/generic, virtual/actual, investigational, and parallel import relationships.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Low FMM makes this less concerning than a mature resource break. The affected concept is business/regulatory relevant, but the old shape was ambiguous and no quick path-specific production evidence was found.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an Identifier object is not a valid R6 crossReference backbone, and migration may require choosing product reference versus coded concept semantics.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial. A legacy identifier field could be retained alongside the typed relationship, but it would preserve ambiguity and allow conflicting old/new related-product representations.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: Agree with the existing Medium impact and Partial alternative judgment.

findings.title: manufacturingBusinessOperation was replaced by operation with changed children and authorization handling

oldState.summary: R4 had a 0..* manufacturingBusinessOperation backbone with operationType, authorisationReferenceNumber, effectiveDate, confidentialityIndicator, manufacturer, and regulator.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 carried manufacturing/administrative operation details directly on the product, including authorization reference number and regulator.

newState.summary: R6 has a 0..* operation backbone with type CodeableReference(ActivityDefinition|PlanDefinition), effectiveDate Period, organization references, and confidentialityIndicator; authorization/regulator details appear to belong in RegulatedAuthorization.
newState.narrativeMd: `operation` keeps the broad process concept but changes several child names and types. `operation.type` can reference plans/activities; `operation.organization` replaces manufacturer-like organizations; `RegulatedAuthorization` is the R6 authorization resource.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element definition text in R6 describes the same manufacturing or administrative process, but R6 uses a shorter name and shifts authorization concepts toward `RegulatedAuthorization`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Old `manufacturingBusinessOperation` elements are rejected by R6. Even after renaming to `operation`, some children need type changes (`dateTime` to `Period`, `CodeableConcept` to `CodeableReference`) and some authorization/regulator data has no direct child in `operation`.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Manufacturing operations and regulatory authorizations are important for compliance, inspections, and supply chain traceability.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal of separating manufacturing or administrative processes from regulated authorization details and allowing operation definitions to reference reusable activities or plans is plausible. A retained alias could preserve old JSON for many instances, but it would leave overlapping operation models in the base resource and would still require a policy for authorization number and regulator data. With those material tradeoffs, the R6 break is probably justified.
justification.inferredGoal: Normalize manufacturing/administrative operations and connect regulated authorization details through `RegulatedAuthorization`.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep deprecated `manufacturingBusinessOperation` while adding normalized `operation` and `RegulatedAuthorization` relationships.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have retained `manufacturingBusinessOperation` as a deprecated backbone and introduced `operation` plus links to `RegulatedAuthorization`. This would help old instances validate during transition. The alternative is partial because old and new operation records could describe the same process differently, authorization data could be duplicated between product and authorization resources, and the deprecated representation might never disappear.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old operation data but duplicates process and authorization facts across overlapping models.

evidence.detail: R4 has the manufacturing business operation backbone.
R6 has `operation` as a manufacturing or administrative process backbone.
R6 `operation.type` is CodeableReference targeting ActivityDefinition or PlanDefinition.
R6 `RegulatedAuthorization` can authorize products and carries type, status, holder, and regulator details.

examples.examplesMd: The example shows only the in-resource part of the migration. The authorization number and regulator likely require a related `RegulatedAuthorization` or extension, depending on local semantics.

findings.narrativeMd: The manufacturing operation model changed enough that a simple path rename is insufficient. Implementers must handle new type domains, period semantics, and data that moved out of the product resource.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 operation backbones are invalid in R6 under their old path. Some old values can be represented in R6 (`operationType` as `type.concept`, `manufacturer` as `organization`), but authorization number and regulator are not preserved by a local element-only transform.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map `manufacturingBusinessOperation` to `operation`; convert `operationType` to `operation.type.concept` unless a PlanDefinition or ActivityDefinition is available; convert a dateTime to an appropriate Period policy; map manufacturers to `organization`; migrate authorization reference and regulator data to `RegulatedAuthorization` or a governed extension. Include tests for date-only, dateTime, multiple manufacturers, and regulator-present cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A deprecated alias could have avoided immediate JSON breakage, but R6 seems to have intentionally separated operational process from regulatory authorization. That model is more expressive but requires graph-level migration.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `manufacturingBusinessOperation` becomes R6 `operation`, with child changes: operation type moves from CodeableConcept to CodeableReference(ActivityDefinition|PlanDefinition), effective date changes from dateTime to Period, manufacturer is generalized to organization, and local authorization/regulator details move toward `RegulatedAuthorization`. Old instances are not valid after a simple rename and some data needs model-aware migration. The R6 goal is nevertheless coherent: separate the process/activity from regulatory authorization records and allow reusable activity/plan definitions. Keeping the full R4 backbone as an alias would duplicate operation and authorization facts.
keyEvidence: R4 `manufacturingBusinessOperation` has operationType, authorisationReferenceNumber, effectiveDate dateTime, confidentialityIndicator, manufacturer, and regulator.
R6 `MedicinalProductDefinition.operation` has type CodeableReference(ActivityDefinition|PlanDefinition), effectiveDate Period, organization, and confidentialityIndicator.
R6 `RegulatedAuthorization` contains subject, identifier, type, status, validityPeriod, holder, regulator, and case elements for authorization/procedure details.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use reduces the standards-stability burden. Manufacturing and authorization data are compliance-relevant, but the checked evidence supports medicinal-product regulatory relevance generally rather than established use of this exact R4 backbone.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: old backbone names and child value shapes are rejected or need conversion; runtime/API/codegen paths also change.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial. A deprecated `manufacturingBusinessOperation` could preserve old JSON temporarily, but it would overlap with `operation` and `RegulatedAuthorization` and require precedence rules for duplicated authorization and process facts.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: Agree with the existing High impact and Partial alternative judgment, while judging the break proportionate under the fresh FMM-informed review.

findings.title: specialDesignation backbone was removed from the product resource

oldState.summary: R4 had a 0..* `specialDesignation` backbone for orphan/minor-use designations, indications, status, dates, and species.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 represented special regulatory designations locally under the product.

newState.summary: No `specialDesignation` element exists on R6 MedicinalProductDefinition; similar authorization/designation concepts are represented by RegulatedAuthorization and ClinicalUseDefinition links.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 `RegulatedAuthorization.type` can represent authorization/designation type such as orphan drug designation, and `RegulatedAuthorization.indication` can point to `ClinicalUseDefinition`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 `RegulatedAuthorization` definitions mention orphan drug designation and include intended use, indication, status, region, holder, and regulator, but there is no direct product-contained successor for every old child.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances with `specialDesignation` are invalid in R6 after only a resource rename. Migration requires creating separate authorization/designation records and may need manual handling for old fields such as `species` or indication references.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Special designations can drive regulatory incentives, restrictions, and clinical/regulatory interpretation.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Moving designations into a generalized regulated authorization model is a reasonable design direction, especially for product, package, substance, and device authorization consistency. A deprecated inline backbone would reduce immediate breakage, but it would not fully solve mapping of indication, species, and authorization semantics and would compete with the R6 authorization resource. The tradeoffs are substantial enough that the break is probably justified.
justification.inferredGoal: Move special designations into a generalized regulated authorization model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated `specialDesignation` while adding a generalized `RegulatedAuthorization` designation representation.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could have kept `specialDesignation` on the product as a deprecated backbone while adding `RegulatedAuthorization` links for the normalized model. This preserves old inline data but creates duplicate places for designation type, status, dates, indications, and regulators. Such duplicate same-domain representations have high long-term interoperability risk because producers and consumers may choose different locations indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves inline designation data but duplicates designation and authorization facts across product-contained and separate resources.

evidence.detail: R6 authorization type definition includes examples such as orphan drug designation.
R6 can link authorization indications to `ClinicalUseDefinition`.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example creates a separate resource and is not a complete authoritative mapping for every old child, especially species and indication choice values.

findings.narrativeMd: `specialDesignation` is a high-value local backbone that disappears from the product resource. The likely R6 representation is a separate regulated authorization/designation resource, so old inline data becomes graph data.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old inline designation content is old-valid/new-invalid. R6 authorization resources can be projected back to R4 only by choosing which authorizations count as product special designations and by flattening linked indications, which is not guaranteed lossless.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Create `RegulatedAuthorization` records for special designations, link them to the migrated product in `subject`, map designation type/status/date/intendedUse where possible, and represent structured indications with `ClinicalUseDefinition` when needed. Flag species and ambiguous indication references for review.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The old backbone could have been retained as deprecated, but that would duplicate the generalized authorization model. The R6 design likely improves consistency across product, package, substance, and device authorizations but imposes graph-level migration.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The R6 destination is inferred from related StructureDefinitions; an official ConceptMap would materially improve confidence.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 had an inline `specialDesignation` backbone for orphan/minor-use designations, indications, status, dates, and species. R6 removes that local backbone; the closest destination is a separate `RegulatedAuthorization` for designation/authorization concepts with possible `ClinicalUseDefinition` indications. This is a meaningful migration burden and may need domain judgment for fields such as species. Still, modeling designations as regulated authorizations is a reasonable base-design goal, and retaining a parallel inline designation structure would create competing places for the same authorization facts.
keyEvidence: R4 `MedicinalProduct.specialDesignation` contains identifier, type, intendedUse, indication[x], status, date, and species.
R6 MedicinalProductDefinition has no `specialDesignation` element.
R6 `RegulatedAuthorization.type` definition explicitly includes orphan drug designation and has subject, indication, intendedUse, status, validityPeriod, holder, and regulator fields.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Low FMM softens the compatibility expectation, but this path is regulatory/public-health relevant. The judgment stays below Revisit because the R6 regulated-authorization model provides a plausible destination and a less-breaking inline alternative has substantial duplication risk.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances with inline `specialDesignation` are invalid in R6 and require creation or linking of separate authorization/use resources.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial. Keeping a deprecated inline `specialDesignation` would preserve old instances, but it would duplicate designation type, status, indication, dates, and regulator/authorization semantics across product and RegulatedAuthorization resources.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: Partially agree with the existing High impact and Partial alternative judgment; the impact is real, but FMM 0 and the explicit RegulatedAuthorization destination make the break probably acceptable.

findings.title: Several local elements were renamed, including productClassification, paediatricUseIndicator, and name substructures

oldState.narrativeMd: These elements are valid R4 paths and would often appear in generated model properties and FHIRPath expressions.

newState.summary: R6 uses `classification`, `pediatricUseIndicator`, `name.part`, and `name.usage` for the corresponding concepts.
newState.narrativeMd: The concepts mostly persist, but their serialized element names and generated property names change. Additional type/binding changes on some children are covered by separate findings.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The definitions and child structures match closely enough to identify these as renames. `paediatricUseIndicator` is also a spelling change from British to US spelling.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Each old path is invalid in R6. Although most values can be moved mechanically, systems using generated properties, JSONPath/FHIRPath, database columns, or search extraction keyed by the R4 names will break until updated.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Classification, pediatric-use, and name-usage data can be relevant to product selection and jurisdiction/language display.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal of shorter and more consistent naming is understandable, but these are mostly path-name changes for concepts that remain recognizable. Keeping `productClassification`, `paediatricUseIndicator`, `name.namePart`, and `name.countryLanguage` would still meet the substantive data-model goals with clearer definitions and aliases. Because the less-breaking option has modest long-term cost and avoids hard wire-level failures, this break was probably avoidable.
justification.inferredGoal: Improve terminology and naming consistency in the product definition resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the R4 element names and improve definitions, aliases, and implementation guidance rather than changing wire paths.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would simply keep the existing R4 element names while updating their definitions, examples, and implementation guidance to match R6 terminology. This avoids duplicate representations because it does not add parallel old and new fields. The main cost is that R6 would carry a few nonoptimal legacy names, including the British spelling `paediatric`, but living with those names is a reasonable compatibility tradeoff.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Leaves longer, less tidy, or British-spelled paths but preserves instance compatibility without duplicate data representations.

examples.examplesMd: The example omits additional type/binding remediation covered in the type-domain and terminology findings.

findings.narrativeMd: These are mostly straightforward path renames, but they are still hard instance breaks because FHIR JSON element names are fixed. The spelling change for pediatric use is especially easy for implementers to miss.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances containing the old element names remain invalid in R6 after a root resource rename. R6 instances can usually be downgraded by reversing the path mapping, except where R6-only child data or binding/type changes are present.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Apply deterministic path rewrites for these fields before validation. Update generated models, FHIRPath, database mappings, search extraction, and UI bindings. Add tests specifically for the British-to-US spelling change and the nested name paths.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Aliases would have avoided wire-level breaks but are uncommon in core FHIR resource definitions and would complicate element identity. A migration map is the practical compatibility mechanism.

freshReview.narrativeMd: Several recognizable concepts were renamed: `productClassification` to `classification`, `paediatricUseIndicator` to `pediatricUseIndicator`, `name.namePart` to `name.part`, and `name.countryLanguage` to `name.usage`. These are hard wire-path and generated-property changes, but the underlying concepts and cardinalities largely remain. Unlike the larger graph remodels, the less-breaking base design is straightforward: keep the R4 element names and improve definitions, aliases, and examples. The low FMM reduces stability pressure, but renaming central product-name/classification fields mostly for tidiness or spelling consistency looks avoidable.
keyEvidence: R4 and R6 definitions for classification, pediatric use, name part, and name usage/country-language are closely matched in meaning and cardinality.
R4 `name.namePart.part` and R6 `name.part.part` both retain 1..1 string; R4 `name.countryLanguage` and R6 `name.usage` retain country, jurisdiction, and language children.
The report's delta and local SD inspection show these are path renames rather than removals of the concepts.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use softens the compatibility concern, but it does not justify avoidable wire-name churn for central name and classification data when the old names could have carried the R6 semantics.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: old element names are rejected by R6 and generated APIs/FHIRPath/database extraction keyed to the old names break.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Yes. Retaining the R4 wire names while updating definitions would preserve compatibility without creating duplicate data locations. The tradeoff is carrying less tidy names, including British spelling, which seems modest.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: Agree with the existing Medium impact and Yes alternative judgment; if anything, the avoidability is clearer than the raw impact score.

findings.title: Several coded/local value elements changed representation shape

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed a raw `Coding` for domain/name-part type and raw strings for special measures.

newState.summary: `domain`, `name.part.type`, and `specialMeasures` are CodeableConcept with example value-set bindings.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 wraps coded values in `CodeableConcept` and turns special measures into coded concepts rather than primitive strings.

facts.newValue: example bindings for medicinal-product-domain, medicinal-product-special-measures, and medicinal-product-name-part-type

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same business concepts remain, but the wire types changed. Coding-to-CodeableConcept can often be wrapped; string-to-CodeableConcept requires coding/text policy.

impact.impactRationaleMd: A JSON `Coding` object is not valid where R6 expects a `CodeableConcept`, and a JSON string is not valid where R6 expects `CodeableConcept`. Strict validators and generated serializers will reject old shapes. Some migration can be lossless (`Coding` -> `CodeableConcept.coding[0]`), but free-text special measures may remain text-only concepts.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Domain and special-measure coding can drive jurisdictional and regulatory interpretation.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Normalizing product attributes to `CodeableConcept` is a reasonable R6 goal because it supports text, multiple codings, and terminology bindings. The change is still a hard JSON shape break, and a transitional model could preserve many old values. However, preserving both `Coding` or `string` and `CodeableConcept` forms in the base resource would materially complicate validation and allow conflicting representations, so the break is probably justified.
justification.inferredGoal: Normalize coded product attributes to CodeableConcept and bind them to example value sets.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Permit legacy `Coding` or `string` shapes alongside new `CodeableConcept` representations through transitional fields.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could have added separate transitional fields for the new `CodeableConcept` values while retaining legacy `Coding` and `string` fields, or otherwise accepted both forms through a more complex model. This is only partial: FHIR cannot cleanly change the type of the same non-choice element while preserving the same JSON shape, and duplicate coded fields would need precedence rules when both old and new forms appear.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Could preserve common old values but introduces validation ambiguity, duplicate coded representations, and conversion rules for text-only measures.

evidence.detail: R6 `specialMeasures` type is `CodeableConcept` with an example value set.

examples.examplesMd: Coding-to-CodeableConcept wrapping can be mechanical. String-to-CodeableConcept is not necessarily semantically coded unless a mapping table supplies a code.

findings.narrativeMd: Several local values became `CodeableConcept`. This is a common migration pattern but a hard JSON shape break. It is especially important for `specialMeasures`, where a primitive string must become either `CodeableConcept.text` or a mapped code.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old Coding and string shapes are invalid in R6. R6 CodeableConcept values can be downgraded to R4 Coding only by choosing one coding and discarding text/additional codings; R6 `specialMeasures` codes can be downgraded to strings only with lossy text extraction.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap old `Coding` values as `CodeableConcept.coding`. For `specialMeasures`, define a controlled mapping from known strings to codes where possible and otherwise populate `text`. Test multiple codings, text-only values, and unknown legacy strings.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: R6 could have used choice elements such as `specialMeasures[x]`, but that would preserve multiple representations indefinitely. Standardizing on CodeableConcept is cleaner but not wire-compatible.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `domain` and `name.namePart.type` move from Coding to CodeableConcept, while `specialMeasures` moves from string to CodeableConcept. Old JSON shapes are invalid at the corresponding R6 paths, although Coding values can usually be wrapped losslessly and string values can often become CodeableConcept.text. Normalizing these elements to CodeableConcept gives room for text, multiple codings, and terminology bindings. Supporting both legacy primitive/Coding shapes and CodeableConcept in base R6 would create awkward duplicate or choice-like representations on existing non-choice elements.
keyEvidence: R4 `domain` and `name.namePart.type` are Coding; R6 `domain` and `name.part.type` are CodeableConcept with example bindings.
R4 `specialMeasures` is string; R6 `specialMeasures` is CodeableConcept with an example special-measures value set.
The element definitions preserve the same business concepts while changing the wire type.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use lowers the concern, and the most common Coding-to-CodeableConcept migration is mechanical. Regulatory interpretation of domain and special measures still makes the path nontrivial, especially for free text.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: Coding objects and strings are not valid CodeableConcept values at the R6 paths.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial. Transitional legacy fields or a choice-style design could preserve more old values, but they would add duplicate coded representations and conflict/precedence rules when both forms are populated.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: Agree with the existing Medium impact and Partial alternative judgment.

findings.title: Name usage language now has a required all-languages binding

oldState.summary: R4 language was 1..1 CodeableConcept with no local binding in the MedicinalProduct StructureDefinition.

binding.description: No binding present on the local R4 element.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 required a language concept when a countryLanguage backbone was present, but did not constrain the code system/value set in this StructureDefinition.

newState.summary: R6 language is 1..1 CodeableConcept with required binding to all-languages.

binding.description: IETF language tag for a human language

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R6 ValueSet compose includes `urn:ietf:bcp:47`. No full expansion or official R4-to-R6 terminology diff was used.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 requires language codings to come from the all-languages value set, which is based on BCP 47 language tags.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The language child is structurally preserved under the renamed name-usage backbone, with the same 1..1 cardinality and CodeableConcept type.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances using arbitrary local language codes could become invalid after migration to `name.usage.language`. If legacy data already uses BCP 47 language tags, the binding should not be disruptive; the risk is data-dependent.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Language affects display, labeling, and jurisdictional product-name interpretation.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Standardizing product-name language to BCP 47 is a strong interoperability goal, and language is a domain where required bindings are often defensible. A weaker binding would be less breaking for local R4 code systems, but it would not provide the same assurance that consumers can interpret the language code. Because the alternative preserves some legacy data at the cost of a material interoperability guarantee, the strengthening is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Use an extensible or preferred BCP 47 binding, or grandfather legacy local language codings during transition.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have used an extensible or preferred binding on `name.usage.language`, or allowed a transition period for known legacy language systems. That would keep more R4 instances valid after path migration. It is partial because consumers could no longer rely on BCP 47 language tags for display, indexing, or localization, and local code systems would still need mapping for broad interoperability.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves more legacy language codes but weakens reliable language processing and display interoperability.

evidence.detail: R4 element has CodeableConcept type and no binding.
R6 element has required binding to `ValueSet/all-languages|6.0.0-ballot4`.

examples.examplesMd: The old invalid-in-R6 example is plausible for a local code system. Actual impact depends on whether deployed R4 data already used BCP 47 codes.

findings.narrativeMd: The name-language element is still required within each usage row, but R6 adds a required terminology binding. This is a conformance hardening, not just a rename.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance with a local language code can be valid in R4 and invalid in R6 after path migration. R6 language content can be represented in R4 because R4 had no local binding, so the main risk is R4-to-R6 validation.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Normalize legacy language concepts to BCP 47 tags before R6 validation. Maintain a mapping table for known local language systems and flag unmapped values for terminology review. Include tests for `en`, regional tags such as `en-US`, text-only concepts, and local code-system values.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: An extensible binding would have been more tolerant of legacy codes, but a required BCP 47 binding is a reasonable interoperability constraint for language. Cross-version transforms should do the compatibility work.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: No terminology expansion service was run; the value set compose was inspected locally.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The language child remains a 1..1 CodeableConcept under the renamed name-usage backbone, but R6 adds a required binding to `all-languages`. R4 instances that used local, non-BCP-47 language codes may become invalid after path migration; instances already using standard language tags should migrate cleanly. A required common language binding is a reasonable interoperability goal for display, indexing, and localization, and weakening it would reduce the assurance that consumers can interpret product-name language.
keyEvidence: R4 `MedicinalProduct.name.countryLanguage.language` is 1..1 CodeableConcept with no local binding in the StructureDefinition.
R6 `MedicinalProductDefinition.name.usage.language` is 1..1 CodeableConcept with required binding to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/all-languages|6.0.0-ballot4`.
R6 country and jurisdiction siblings keep example/common jurisdiction bindings, confirming the language change is a binding-strength change on the renamed backbone.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use softens the effect, and no quick evidence showed legacy local language code prevalence. The field still affects regulated product-name display, so a data-dependent compatibility break remains plausible.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: after path migration, CodeableConcepts without a coding in the required all-languages value set can fail validation.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial. An extensible or preferred binding would preserve more local R4 codings, but would weaken reliable language processing and cross-system display semantics.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: Agree with the existing Potential hard break and Partial alternative judgment, though the fresh review treats the practical impact as data-dependent.

findings.title: R6 adds optional product lifecycle status as a modifier plus other R6-only content

oldState.summary: R4 MedicinalProduct had no local product record `status` modifier element and lacked the R6-only content fields listed in this finding.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 product lifecycle/record status was not represented as a local modifier on `MedicinalProduct`.

newState.summary: R6 adds `status` 0..1 CodeableConcept with `isModifier=true`, plus optional fields such as version, statusDate, description, route, indication, code, ingredient, impurity, comprisedOf, and characteristic.

binding.description: The lifecycle status of an artifact.

newState.narrativeMd: `status` modifies interpretation because retired/draft/unknown product-definition records should not be treated like active records. Other added fields carry R6-only product data.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: These elements are present in the R6 successor and have no same local R4 product element.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Optional additions do not make old R4 instances invalid in R6. They do matter for R6 consumers and R6-to-R4 conversion: `status` is a modifier and must not be silently ignored, and several R6-only fields have no direct R4 location.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Ignoring a product-definition lifecycle status such as retired or draft can cause business processes to treat a product definition as usable when it should not be.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding lifecycle status and richer product-definition content is a reasonable R6 evolution. The `status` modifier creates a processing obligation for R6 consumers, but the fields are optional and therefore are not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design change. The reported risk is mainly runtime interpretation and R6-to-R4 downgrade fidelity, so the backward-compatible-alternative question does not apply in the same way as for removed, renamed, or narrowed R4 content.
justification.inferredGoal: Add lifecycle management and additional definitional product attributes.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable; these are optional R6 additions and do not make R4 instances invalid in the R4-to-R6 direction.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking base R6 alternative is needed for R4-to-R6 instance compatibility because optional additions already preserve old instances with respect to these fields. Making `status` non-modifier would reduce implementer burden but would also allow unsafe ignoring of lifecycle state. Extensions or sidecar records for R6-to-R4 downgrade are migration mitigations, not evidence of a different base R6 design that was needed to preserve R4 instances.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Optional additions preserve R4-to-R6 base compatibility; R6-to-R4 fidelity remains a separate conversion concern.

evidence.detail: R6 adds optional direct coded ingredients.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 fragment is valid-shape illustrative content that has no direct R4 `MedicinalProduct` fields for `status`, `route`, or `characteristic`.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 introduces more authoring and lifecycle metadata. The most important addition is `status`, because it is explicitly a modifier. Systems that consume R6 product definitions must process it rather than treating it as harmless descriptive data.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is not an R4-to-R6 validation break for old instances because the fields are optional. It is a runtime and round-trip break for R6-to-R4: R4 lacks direct fields for these additions, and ignoring `status` can change business meaning.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: When converting R6 to R4, preserve `status` and other R6-only content in governed extensions or sidecar records if round-trip fidelity matters. R6 consumers should add tests that retired/draft/unknown status values are surfaced to business logic.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Optional additions are the usual backward-compatible approach, but a modifier addition still creates processing obligations for R6 consumers. The alternative of a non-modifier status would be less disruptive but less safe.

freshReview.narrativeMd: This finding is mainly about optional R6 additions: lifecycle `status` as a modifier plus version, statusDate, description, route, indication, code, ingredient, impurity, comprisedOf, characteristic, and related content. Optional additions do not make R4 instances invalid in the R4-to-R6 direction. The modifier status is important for R6 consumers and R6-to-R4 downgrades can lose information, but that is a forward-use and reverse-conversion concern rather than a break in existing R4 content.
keyEvidence: R4 MedicinalProduct has no local product-record `status` modifier element.
R6 `MedicinalProductDefinition.status` is 0..1 CodeableConcept with `isModifier=true` because status can indicate the record should not be treated as valid.
The other listed R6 fields are optional additions on MedicinalProductDefinition.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use further reduces concern. Since these are optional additions, low maturity and trial-use status do not create a reason to revisit the base design for R4-to-R6 compatibility.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6-only fields, especially modifier `status`, require handling when downgrading or consuming R6, but there is no old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 mechanism.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Not applicable. Optional R6 additions already preserve old R4 instances. Making `status` non-modifier would be less burdensome but could make unsafe lifecycle states easier to ignore.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: Disagree with the existing Medium/High runtime framing as an R4-to-R6 break; agree that no less-breaking alternative is needed for old-instance compatibility.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: No local non-inherited constraints/invariants were found on R4 `MedicinalProduct` or R6 `MedicinalProductDefinition` elements. DomainResource constraints were excluded as inherited base-artifact scope.
No fixed values, pattern values, or default values were found on local elements in either StructureDefinition.
No local `minValue`, `maxValue`, `maxLength`, or regex-style value limits were identified.
No local slicing discriminators or slice rules were found on the assigned product resource structures.

No retained same-path local element showed a material min increase or max decrease. Cardinality effects introduced by renamed/rewrapped backbones, such as mandatory `contact.contact` and `crossReference.product`, are covered in findings rather than counted here as unchanged.

`attachedDocument`, `masterFile`, and `clinicalTrial` retain their reference target profiles. Reference-target changes for package, pharmaceutical product, operation, and split resources are covered in findings.

Most newly added R6 bindings are example or preferred and are not hard base validation breaks. The required local binding on `name.usage.language` is reported separately. No terminology expansion comparison was performed.
No material local summary-flag break was identified beyond new or reshaped elements already reported. Inherited summary flag changes on base `modifierExtension` elements were excluded.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds several optional descriptive/product-definition fields
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Optional additions such as `version`, `statusDate`, `description`, `code`, `route`, `indication`, `ingredient`, `impurity`, `comprisedOf`, `characteristic`, and `name.type` do not make existing R4 instances invalid by themselves.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: They are important for R6 authoring and for R6-to-R4 round-tripping; preserve them with extensions or related resources when downgrading.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Many R6 CodeableConcept elements add example bindings
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Example bindings on elements such as `type`, `domain`, `combinedPharmaceuticalDoseForm`, `legalStatusOfSupply`, and classification/package/contact concepts guide terminology use but do not prohibit other codes in base validation.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Implementers may still want terminology mapping for better interoperability, but these example bindings are not hard conformance breaks.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Successor artifact status changed from draft to active
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The StructureDefinition publication status change does not directly invalidate instances. It does signal that the R6 successor is more mature than the R4 draft resource.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Treat R4-to-R6 migration as moving from a draft medicinal-product model to the active R6 product-definition model, but do not classify this status change itself as an instance break.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: combinedPharmaceuticalDoseForm definition now clarifies distinction from administrable dose form
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The type and cardinality remain CodeableConcept 0..1; the change is explanatory rather than a direct wire-format break.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Review business rules that previously treated the combined pharmaceutical dose form as the administrable dose form; R6 points to `AdministrableProductDefinition.administrableDoseForm` for the latter.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: Detailed package data formerly linked from `MedicinalProduct.packagedMedicinalProduct` likely migrates to `PackagedProductDefinition.packageFor`; that resource needs its own R4-to-R6 assessment.
Pharmaceutical/administrable product aspects formerly referenced from `pharmaceuticalProduct` may migrate here, especially dose form and route details.
R6 `MedicinalProductDefinition.comprisedOf` references manufactured items/devices, and R4 pharmaceutical/manufactured product data may need transformation into this resource.
R6 `Ingredient.for` can point to the migrated product or related product-definition resources; ingredient migration cannot be completed from the product artifact alone.
R4 indication/contraindication/interaction/undesirable-effect resources and special designation indications appear to be consolidated or linked through R6 `ClinicalUseDefinition`.
R4 special designation and manufacturing authorization/regulator data likely migrates to `RegulatedAuthorization`; a dedicated assessment is needed.
Inherited base changes such as base language binding, modifierExtension summary flags, and dom-* constraint expression changes were intentionally excluded from this local report.
Several R6 mappings use `CodeableReference`; datatype-level representability and codegen behavior should be handled by the datatype report.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 diff, ConceptMap, or migration guide was available in the local inputs. Successor and split-resource mappings are inferred from StructureDefinitions and package indexes.
